Nothing is hung or dead, and the CPU quota is still the bottleneck. I made one change: two runs were sharing a CPU core, so I moved one of them to a free core.

**Resources**
- **CPU:** 31.1 of the 32 quota cores in use (measured over 30 s). 63 % of time slices were throttled, so the quota is what limits speed. Host load is 50 on 256 cores.
- **Memory:** 129.6 / 137.4 GB used in the account's memory limit, but only 40.4 GB is real process memory; the other 85.8 GB is file cache the system can free. No out-of-memory kills.
- **GPU:** my 7 runs are on GPU3 (5) and GPU5 (2) and barely load them. Other users have GPU6 at 99 %, GPU1 at 71 %, GPU4 at 59 %, and 38.5 GB in use on GPU0. GPU is not the limit.
- **Disk:** /raid has 2.6 TB free.

**Queues**
- **FEBio:** 33 waiting (oldest since 04:06, 7.4 h), 11 running, 2378 done, 2 failed.
- **Throughput:** 3 runs finished in each of the 09h and 10h hours, and 6 so far in the 11h hour (27 min).
- **Task queue:** empty, nothing running, 1 done, 5 failed (the same five `gate2_*` tasks as last hour).

**Health:** all 11 FEBio logs were written within the last 20 s. All tmux services are up; the four one-off services (physio_v3, physio_rot, rot_chain, nas_archive) are marked finished.

**Action:** `p081_gpu3/w_flexion` (pid 2908188) was sharing core 18 with `p066/w_flexion`. I moved all its threads to cores 22, 26, 28, 31 (22 was idle and unassigned). I changed no settings and restarted no services; the scheduler stays up because CPU split runs are in progress.

**Needs a person:**
- The scheduler keeps assigning cores that running split runs already hold. This is the 4th time today, and it needs a code fix in h19/h31.
- The only way to clear the 33 waiting runs faster is a larger CPU quota; at the current rate they take about 8–10 h.
